newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on political uncertainty. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on political uncertainty. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: Nervous selling, triggered by Patna High Court's rejection of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav's bail application, pushed down Delhi share prices at close on Thursday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index closed 9.10 points lower at 884.31 after surging to 900.12 earlier.
(Corrects to make clear closing figure was 884.31, not 900.12.)
Traders said the possibility of instability in the ruling United Front government, as a result of fresh political developments, had triggered late selling.
"The fall in heavy-weighted stocks seems to be temporary, due to nervous offerings and should recover soon," said Sanjay Kaul of stock brokerage Sanjay Kaul and Co.
The Patna High Court on Thursday rejected Yadav's application in a $280 million corruption scandal case for "anticipatory bail" to avert arrest by federal police.
Yadav says he is innocent in the case which has divided Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition, which is debating whether to admit Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party.
"Short selling by bear operators who anticipate stock prices might react further dampened sentiments, particularly towards the end of the session," said one Delhi broker.
Reliance Industries fell 8.35 rupees to 353 after surging to 365.50 in early trade, brokers said.
Tisco lost 2.35 rupees to 213.40 after rallying to 218.80.
State Bank of India was down 5.30 rupees to 325.90.
Hero Honda Motors slipped 6.00 rupees to 608 rupees.
Larsen and Toubro fell 3.10 rupees to 266.50.
